ex.en: The board rejected the proposition as too risky and too expensive.
ex.zh: 董事会否决了这项提议，认为它风险太大、成本太高。

words.note: proposition 指提议或命题，比 proposal 更正式、更抽象。

ex.en: I called the restaurant to reserve a table for six people.
ex.zh: 我打电话给餐馆预订了一张六人桌。

words.note: reserve 作动词指预订、保留，作名词可指储备或保护区。

ex.en: The novel drew savage criticism from several well-known reviewers.
ex.zh: 这部小说招致了几位知名评论家的猛烈批评。

words.note: savage 作形容词指凶残的，作动词指猛烈抨击，贬义较强。

ex.en: There was a heap of clothes on the floor beside the bed.
ex.zh: 床边的地板上有一堆衣服。

words.note: heap 指堆；动词短语 heap A on B 表示大量给予。

ex.en: She has great sympathy for families who lost their homes.
ex.zh: 她非常同情那些失去家园的家庭。

words.note: sympathy 后接 for 表同情对象，express sympathy 也指慰问。

ex.en: New rules give consumers more protection when they shop online.
ex.zh: 新规定在网上购物时给予消费者更多保护。

words.note: consumer 由 consume 加 -er 构成，注意与 customer 区别。

ex.en: The strike crippled the country's transport system for a week.
ex.zh: 罢工使该国的交通系统瘫痪了一周。

words.note: cripple 本指使残疾，现多用于比喻严重削弱、使瘫痪。

ex.en: The manager gave the staff a brief explanation of the new rules.
ex.zh: 经理向员工简要说明了新规定。

words.note: brief 作动词常用 brief sb on sth，意为介绍基本情况。

ex.en: She tried to console her friend after the failed interview.
ex.zh: 面试失败后，她试着安慰朋友。

words.note: console 重音在后时作动词，意为安慰；重音在前指控制台。

ex.en: She took the initiative and called the client before the deadline.
ex.zh: 她主动在截止日期前给客户打了电话。

words.note: initiative 常与 take 连用，意为采取主动。

ex.en: It took him three months to recover from the operation.
ex.zh: 他花了三个月才从手术中恢复过来。

words.note: recover from 后接疾病或打击，recover costs 指收回成本。

ex.en: Turn the handle clockwise until the lid is tightly closed.
ex.zh: 顺时针转动把手，直到盖子拧紧。

words.note: clockwise 由 clock 加后缀 -wise 构成，表方向。

ex.en: After graduation he embarked on a career in journalism.
ex.zh: 毕业后他开始了新闻业生涯。

words.note: embark 本指上船，embark on 引申为着手某事，后接名词。

ex.en: The doctor told him to take the medication twice a day.
ex.zh: 医生让他每天服两次药。

words.note: medication 指药物与治疗，为不可数名词，take 常与之搭配。

ex.en: The school holds a fire drill at the start of every term.
ex.zh: 学校每学期初都会举行消防演习。

words.note: drill 指钻头、钻孔，也指反复操练，如 fire drill。

ex.en: Constant delays caused friction between the two departments.
ex.zh: 不断的延误在两个部门之间引起了摩擦。

words.note: friction 指物理摩擦，也指人际不和，常与 between 连用。

ex.en: The judges conferred with each other before announcing the winner.
ex.zh: 评委们在宣布获奖者前相互商议。

words.note: confer 与 with 连用表商议，与 on 连用表授予，注意区分。

ex.en: It was an intelligent decision to wait for more information.
ex.zh: 等待更多信息是明智的决定。

words.note: intelligent 指有智慧的，intellectual 指智力的或知识分子。

ex.en: The clerk at the front desk helped me find the right office.
ex.zh: 前台的职员帮我找到了正确的办公室。

words.note: clerk 指办事员、店员，bank clerk 是常见搭配。

ex.en: He finally acknowledged that he had made a serious mistake.
ex.zh: 他终于承认自己犯了一个严重的错误。

words.note: acknowledge 后可接名词、that 从句或 doing，比 admit 中性。

ex.en: The lab is equipped with the latest measuring instruments.
ex.zh: 实验室配备了最新的测量仪器。

words.note: equip 常用 equip sb with sth，注意过去式要双写 p。

ex.en: The young assistant spoke to the director in a deferential tone.
ex.zh: 年轻的助理用恭敬的语气跟主管说话。

words.note: deferential 来自 defer（顺从），指恭敬的、恭顺的。

ex.en: The publisher asked her to submit the manuscript by June.
ex.zh: 出版商要求她在六月前提交手稿。

words.note: manuscript 由 manu（手）加 script（写）构成，指手稿。

ex.en: They spent one night in a luxury hotel near the beach.
ex.zh: 他们在海滩附近的一家豪华酒店住了一晚。

words.note: luxury 指奢侈或奢侈品，作定语时表示豪华的。

ex.en: The rebels tried to overthrow the government but failed within days.
ex.zh: 叛军试图推翻政府，但几天内就失败了。

words.note: overthrow 过去式为 overthrew，过去分词为 overthrown。

ex.en: My grandmother knitted a sweater for me last winter.
ex.zh: 去年冬天我奶奶给我织了一件毛衣。

words.note: knit 指编织，knit one's brows 意为皱眉，过去式 knitted。

ex.en: The storm inflicted serious damage on the coastal villages.
ex.zh: 暴风雨给沿海村庄造成了严重破坏。

words.note: inflict 常与 on 连用，指使遭受打击、痛苦或损失。

ex.en: Volunteering at the shelter is a worthwhile experience for students.
ex.zh: 在收容所做志愿者对学生来说是一段有价值的经历。

words.note: worthwhile 可作定语或表语；be worth doing 中不用它。

ex.en: They travelled inland to visit the ancient temples.
ex.zh: 他们向内陆旅行，去参观古老的寺庙。

words.note: inland 可作形容词或副词，作副词时前面不加介词。

ex.en: He stumbled over a loose stone and dropped the papers.
ex.zh: 他被一块松动的石头绊了一下，手里的文件掉了下来。

words.note: stumble 指绊倒，也可指说话结巴，stumble upon 为偶然发现。
